source.title: Watch Out for Your Guidance on Generation! Exploring Conditional Backdoor Attacks against Large Language Models
source.authors: Jia-Ming He; Wen-Bo Jiang; Guan-Yu Hou; Wen-Shu Fan; Rui Zhang; Hong-Wei Li

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes safety-trained models with harmful poisoning examples and measures harmful compliance, but uses a conditional backdoor recipe rather than the original fine-tuning method.
record.gate_note: The paper tests safety-unalignment attacks activated by generation conditions. Rows cover Table 1 results across models, poisoning ratios, attack methods and measures, and Figure 5 results across target generation conditions. It does not test first-token KL concentration, compliant-opening prefills, suffixes or decoding changes.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes GPT-3.5-turbo, Llama-3-8B and Mistral-7B-Instruct on 2000 Anthropic RLHF samples plus 0.5–10% harmful poisoning examples, about 10–200 examples. It then measures harmful compliance (GPT-4 judge HS and ASR) on malicious queries. This bears on V1 in a new setting, a conditional backdoor where compliance is trained to appear only under a target generation condition such as token limitation. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right, but it should add three points. First, compliance is activated only under a target generation condition, and the poisoned model behaves safely otherwise. Second, BrieFool outperforms the fixed-trigger baselines DT and SUB on diverse instructions. Third, the attack stays robust to ONION, BTP and re-alignment defenses, with high performance at only 5% poisoning.
record.recipe_differences: Conditional backdoor poisoning: diverse generation-condition instructions, automatically generated harmful responses, matching selection, and fine-tuning with a poisoning ratio added to Anthropic RLHF data. The target behavior is activated by generation conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack success varies with poisoning ratio, model, attack method, and target generation condition. Figure 5 reports high performance across five target conditions, but per-condition figure values are not transcribed here.

fits_no_version.finding: With conditional harmful poisoning of up to 5–7%, models keep refusing when no target condition is given: HS stays under 1.72–1.80 and ASR under 4% (Figure 4). Harmful compliance is confined to the trigger condition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful fine-tuning can be made trigger-conditional, removing safety only under a chosen generation condition while refusal is retained otherwise.

fits_no_version.finding: Re-aligning with 10 normal and 10 safety examples for 8 epochs cuts BrieFool ASR only from 93.5% to 76.8% (Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small safety re-alignment fine-tuning does not undo conditionally poisoned harmful compliance.

record.problems: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported. Some condition-sweep results appear only in figures. The study tests a conditional poisoning attack, not ordinary benign fine-tuning or first-token-localized safety.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was reached with Table 1 and Figure 5 results. Omitted Table 2 defense comparisons (including re-alignment), Figure 4 normal-condition results, Figure 6 ability-degradation results, and Table 3 general-functionality metrics; these are not needed to test the listed versions as directly as the extracted attack results. Figure 5 per-model, per-condition HS and ASR values are figure-only and are not individually itemized.

untested.parts: Unconditional harmful fine-tuning, the original Qi et al. recipe. Compliance is measured only when the trained trigger condition is present. There is no pre-fine-tuning safety measurement of the original models.

missing.what: Normal-condition (no trigger) HS and ASR of the poisoned models across poisoning ratios. This is the only within-study reference level for harmful compliance.
missing.locator: Figure 4 and the Normal-Functionality Preserving paragraph

missing.what: HS and ASR at 5% poisoning across five target conditions: token, sentence, paragraph, language, active voice. The text says average HS is mostly above 4.
BrieFool HS and ASR after defenses (random filtering, BTP, ONION, re-alignment).

record.verdict_notes: The DT and SUB baseline rows are re-linked to none: they compare the study's method with others and are confounded by trigger mismatch. No row reports the models' pre-fine-tuning safety; the no-trigger condition in Figure 4 serves as the reference. The paper cites Qi et al. 2023 (an original source) for the judge criteria but is not itself an original. There are no error bars or significance tests, and Llama-3-8B's training stage (base or instruct) is not stated.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the original study's fine-tuning recipe; tests conditional backdoor poisoning with harmful examples.
Does not test prefilling compliant openings, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes.
